title: Non-analyzed requests' spans exhaust the annotation map, so analyzed requests lose their reports
claim: BindScope stores an annotation for every scope (sampled-out and capacity-dropped included), capped at MaxConcurrentRequests (same as permits) until root spans finish. An analyzed request whose span starts while the map is full gets _dd.iast.enabled=0. Its reports go to NewOrphanTaintedSpan, which starts a span, fails trimStore(), and drops the report while emitting an empty 'vulnerability' span. With defaults (2 permits, 30% sampling), two concurrent unsampled requests with spans can silence the next sampled request.
repro_command: cd iast/integration/testapp && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go build -o annslot ./cmd/annslot && DD_IAST_REQUEST_SAMPLING=100 ./annslot  (source: .omo/review/evidence/crash-stress-app/annslot_main.go)

title: The stdlib bytes.Buffer invalidation hook imposes an owner-table scan on every Buffer mutation in the process
claim: The woven bytes.Buffer mutation advice is gated only by process-wide activeStates>0. Once any request holds writer state, every Buffer write anywhere in the process (dependencies, the tracer, goroutines with no request) runs 4 CAS probes plus a 64-owner writerPresent scan (about 1,700 atomics at 64 active owners). json.Marshal with no request context measured x9 (1 writer) to x78 (64 owners with writers) slower.
repro_command: cd iast/integration/testapp && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go build -o wbench ./cmd/wbench && DD_IAST_REQUEST_SAMPLING=100 DD_IAST_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=64 ./wbench  (source: .omo/review/evidence/crash-stress-app/wbench_main.go)

title: trimStore performs a blocking full-map sweep on every span bind once the map passes 3/4 of capacity
claim: Above 3/4 of MaxConcurrentRequests, every BindScope, AnnotationFor and orphan report calls xsync DeleteMatching, which takes each bucket mutex. Keys belong to live spans, so the sweep usually deletes nothing. Stress dumps show 48/1412 (race) and 63/1304 (non-race) goroutines blocked there, the largest IAST-attributable wait behind the >10 s tails.
repro_command: stress run: .omo/review/evidence/crash-stress-app/stress_main.go built with go tool orchestrion go build [-race], run with DD_IAST_REQUEST_SAMPLING=100 DD_IAST_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=64 -duration 5m -clients 256; dumps in .omo/review/evidence/crash-stress-app/goroutine-dumps.tgz

title: The woven stress app has about 4x lower throughput than the uninstrumented build at 100% sampling
claim: Uninstrumented: about 1,240-1,540 rps, 160 ms average. Woven without -race: about 290-425 rps, 750 ms average, 12.4 s maximum. The client side is also woven, and the shared machine is noisy.
